_note: FICTIONAL EXAMPLE. 'Alex Example' is not a real person. No real data. Input dates are exact; the export coarsens them to the month by default.

reasonable_adjustments.description: After any meeting or appointment, please send me a short written summary of what was agreed and any next steps.
Please hold meetings in a quiet room with good light on the speaker's face. Face-to-face with lip-reading works for me in that setting; captions or written notes also work.
Please allow me extra time to read, think and reply before any decision is needed.
Appointment reminders by text message or email.

channels_that_do_not_work_for_me.in_my_own_words: I cannot pick out the options quickly enough, so I end up in the wrong place.

functional_impact.in_my_own_words: In a quiet room, facing one person, I follow most of what is said by lip-reading, though it tires me. In groups or with background noise I lose the thread quickly. I often realise afterwards that I misheard a detail, so a written note of what was agreed matters to me.
what_helps: A written summary after a meeting
Time to read and reply before decisions
what_does_not_help: Speakers who turn away or cover their mouths
Being expected to answer straight away

variation_over_time.in_my_own_words: With a cold, lip-reading in noisy places becomes much harder and I rely more on written notes.
After long days I need noticeably more time to take in what has been said.
